transcript.content: Hello, please have a seat. What brings you into the clinic today?

I'm here because... well, I just can't bring myself to go near the front windows at work anymore. Or even that part of the street outside. I keep finding excuses to stay in the back room, unpacking boxes or whatever, even though being out on the floor is my actual job.
What is it that frightens or worries you about being near those front windows or that street?

It's just that... the crash keeps popping into my head out of nowhere. I'll be trying to set up displays or something, and suddenly it's like I'm right back there. I can hear that loud bang, and I see the glass coming down all over again. It feels so real, like it's happening right in that moment.
It was about two weeks ago. I was working an overnight shift, and... well, a car just crashed right through the store window. So, this has all been going on ever since that night.
Since the accident, have you felt detached from yourself or like the world around you isn't real?

Yeah, I actually have. Um... sometimes when I'm out on the sales floor, things just feel really off. The lights and the clothing racks will suddenly seem really far away and kind of fake. It's hard to explain, but it almost feels like I’m just watching myself move through the store, instead of actually being there doing it.
